errorCodes.meaning: No such did:webs DID is held by this VTA, or the caller cannot reach its context.
The DID's latest event no longer matches `expectedVersionId`. Re-read it and re-apply the change.
The request would replace no designation, or replace each with one equal to the one in force. Nothing is published.
An additional service uses `#didcomm` or `#tsp`, an id a KERI endpoint reply of the AID establishes, or an id another service in the set uses.
The DID is deactivated. Nothing can be anchored in its log.
The hosting server refused the publication. Nothing was committed; `details.hostError` carries what the server said.

DesignatedService.description: A DID document service entry the AID designates for itself: an ACDC it issues in its own registry, anchored in its key event log, which the host renders into `service`. Not a KERI endpoint reply, which can carry only KERI's own roles and URL schemes. `id` is a fragment relative to the DID. Members other than `id`, `type` and `serviceEndpoint` are carried as the DID document data model allows.

id.description: The service's fragment, such as `#files`. `#didcomm` and `#tsp` are the VTA's own (see `addMediatorService` and `addTspService`), and an id a KERI endpoint reply of the AID already establishes cannot be reused.

serviceEndpoint.description: A URI, a map, or a set of either, as the DID document data model allows.

type.description: The service type, matched by peers on its value, never on `id`.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

alsoKnownAs.description: The designated aliases in force after the update, the DID itself first.

keyAgreementKey.description: The key agreement key in force after the update, in CESR.

keyAgreementKeyId.description: The VTA's id for the key agreement key in force after the update.

sequenceNumber.description: Sequence number of the interaction event that anchors the replacements.

serviceIds.description: Ids of the designated services in force after the update.

versionId.description: That event as `<sequence number>:<SAID>`. A caller intending a further change passes it as `expectedVersionId`.

Response.title: VTA did:webs DIDs Update — response payload

ServiceSet.description: A whole set of designated services, stated in full so that a replacement never depends on what the caller believes is already there.

additional.description: Further services in the set. Absent means none. None may use `#didcomm` or `#tsp`.

mediator.description: Whether `#didcomm`, typed `DIDCommMessaging`, with the VTA's mediator's DID as its endpoint, is in the set.

tsp.description: Whether `#tsp`, typed `TSPTransport`, with the VTA's mediator's DID as its endpoint, is in the set.

schema.description: Replace a did:webs DID's designated services, its key agreement key or its designated aliases. Each replacement is a designation anchored by an interaction event; no key of the key state changes. Alpha.

alsoKnownAs.description: The further aliases to stand from now on, replacing those in force. The DID itself is always designated, first, and is not listed. An empty array withdraws every further alias. Absent leaves the aliases as they are.

expectedVersionId.description: Precondition: the DID's latest event, as `<sequence number>:<SAID>`, that the caller based this change on. Refused with `versionConflict` when the DID has moved on.

rotateKeyAgreementKey.description: Derive a fresh X25519 key agreement key and designate it in place of the current one. Absent or false keeps the current key.

services.description: The designated services to stand from now on, replacing the set in force. Absent leaves the services as they are.
